data.name: Bhutan
data.summary: Bhutan's Income Tax Act 2025 took effect on 1 January 2026: progressive personal rates up to 30% above Nu 3.5M, dividends above Nu 300,000 taxed at 10%, and (per press reports of the Act) no capital gains tax on individuals' non-business assets. No wealth, inheritance or gift tax was found. Practically, Bhutan offers no residence route for a wealthy foreign family; the Gelephu Mindfulness City special region is still being set up. Research is thin (no Big-4 summary exists): low confidence.

regimes.name: Bhutan tax residence
regimes.description: Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025: 10% on dividends above Nu 300,000; gains on personal assets reportedly untaxed.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence under the Income Tax Act 2025 (test not verified). Foreigners rarely obtain long-term residence.

capital_gains.summary: Press reports on the Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025 (in force 1 January 2026) state there is no capital gains tax for individuals selling personal assets outside business use. Treatment of listed shares, foreign securities and real estate was not confirmed from the Act.

succession.name: Bhutan
succession.summary: Bhutan's Inheritance Act 1980 lets a person pass property by written or oral will, with shares for the family fixed by the Act when there is no will. Non-Bhutanese, including foreign spouses and children, cannot inherit land or houses and are shut out of any share of an inheritance. There is no trust or private foundation law.
succession.family_claims: No court-ordered provision for dependants found. Without a will the Act sets the shares of family members in the main house (Ga 4, 5).
succession.foreign_law_note: The Inheritance Act extends to all citizens and persons residing in Bhutan (Ga 1-3). Non-Bhutanese are not entitled to any share of an inheritance (Ga 2-11), and a foreign spouse and children of a Bhutanese may inherit only movables (Ga 6-23). I found no rule letting a foreign resident choose another law.
succession.trust_note: Bhutan is not on the HCCH status table. I found no trust or private foundation statute. Civil society organisations are registered under the Civil Society Organizations Act, which is for non-profit purposes (not retrieved).
open_questions: The Act has not been checked for later amendments or for any protected share of children; a Bhutanese lawyer should confirm whether the will chapter (Ga 7) is subject to the family-share rules.
Confirm there is no trust statute and that no foundation law exists beyond the CSO Act.
